{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "Let $f(x)=- x^{3} + 42 x - 2.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\prime}(x) &= \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(- x^{3} + 42 x - 2\right) \\
&= (-1)\cdot 3\cdot x^{2} + (42)\cdot 1\cdot 1 \\
&= 42 - 3 x^{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f^{\prime}(x)=-6$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
42 - 3 x^{2} &= -6 \\
48 - 3 x^{2} &= 0 \\
- 3 \left(x - 4\right) \left(x + 4\right) &= 0 \\
x &= -4,\,4
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $x>0$, the required coordinate is $x=4.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["dc755ef9-cb44-5175-b229-7f7ea951429f"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "generator" :question-generator/id #uuid "0316d2d2-d2d0-523c-9990-f47eb598f22e" :question-generator/script "generate/scratch/17592186064259.py"} [:db/add 17592186064259 :knowledge-point/question-generator "generator"] {:db/id 17592186064259 :knowledge-point/questions ["3fd03b4b-26b0-57a3-90b6-cf64c012470d"]} [:db/ensure 17592186064259 :knowledge-point/validate]]
